chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was asked: 'Which charity is most superior?' He said: 'That given to a relative who is hostile.'

key_terms.أفضل: Afdal — most superior, most virtuous, most meritorious. Common comparative adjective used to rank religious acts.
key_terms.الصدقة: Sadaqa — voluntary charity, alms-giving. In this hadith it refers to charitable giving (sadaqa) broadly, not just obligatory zakat.
key_terms.الكاشح: Al-kashih — one who harbors enmity in his heart; specifically one who turns away from you with hostility, often referring to a relative who has severed ties or is estranged.
key_terms.ذو الرحم: Dhu al-rahm — one possessing womb/kinship ties; a relative, especially a blood relative.

ai.seo_question: Which type of charity is most superior according to the Prophet Muhammad?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates a prophetic tradition in which the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) was asked about the most meritorious form of charity. The Prophet's answer — that charity given to a hostile relative is the best — reflects the Islamic teaching that moral excellence lies in maintaining ties even when they are strained or severed. In the early Muslim community, the concept of silat al-rahim (maintaining kinship ties) was central to social ethics, and giving to one who has wronged you or cut ties with you was seen as the highest expression of generosity and moral fortitude.
word_analysis: the hostile/the one who severs ties
